title: Count All Words
statement:
Count how many words the whole input holds, across every line.

The input is zero or more lines of text. There is no count line, so keep reading until the input ends. Words are separated by one or more spaces, and a line can be blank or start and end with spaces. Print the total number of words on all the lines, or `0` when there are none.

Input:

```text
the quick brown fox
jumps over
the lazy dog
```

Expected output:

```text
9
```

tests.stdin:
the quick brown fox
jumps over
the lazy dog

a b c d e

   
f

hints: Read one line at a time in a loop that stops when the input runs out.
Split each line into words in a way that ignores extra spaces, then add how many you got to a running total.

python.solution:
import sys
from typing import TextIO


def count_all_words(stream: TextIO) -> int:
    count = 0
    for line in stream:
        count += len(line.split())
    return count


print(count_all_words(sys.stdin))
